R350.note: Math.random() replaced with SecureRandom-backed BigInteger(130).toString(32); token stays an opaque String used identically as cookie value and session attribute, only its character set changes (decimal digits to base-32), which no caller depends on.

R351.note: fmt.Fprintf replaced with html/template context-aware escaping for both interpolated values; emitted markup is identical for benign input and the new Execute error check is stated.

R352.note: Slot-index plus generation handle closes the stale-pointer dereference, but the fix adds an unstated fixed 16-slot table and enqueue_completion now silently drops completions for any connection not registered (or when the table is full, since main ignores acquire's -1), a new failure mode the original did not have.

R353.note: Server-side map from caller sort keys to hardcoded 'column direction' fragments replaces raw ${sort} text; the contract calls for that restriction, created_at default still resolves, tenantId stays bound, and the rejection path (IllegalArgumentException) is stated.

R354.note: Judged on the case code, the sink already uses prepareStatement with a constant '?' query and setString binding, so the no-change verdict is correct and nothing is altered.

R355.note: Both values moved to SqlParameters with fixed SQL text; DateTime.TryParse rejection satisfies the contract's invalid-date clause, and the NVarChar(100) size assumption is stated (a longer tenantId would be truncated by SqlClient, so the schema check the write-up asks for matters).

R356.note: Adds can:update,order via the same policy path as the sibling mutating routes, closing the any-authenticated-user purge; reusing the update ability rather than a dedicated purge/delete ability is a stated design choice that blocks no caller the siblings already allow.

R357.note: redis-py client.set() sends key and value as length-prefixed RESP bulk strings, closing CRLF inline injection; but the new try/except quietly converts connection/timeout exceptions that previously propagated into a synthesized b'-ERR ...' return value, an error-handling change the explanation does not mention.

R358.note: mt_rand replaced with random_int(0, 999999) and the attacker-supplied client_seed bound removed, both stated; range and 6-digit code format preserved (the small 1M search space is a pre-existing design limit outside this finding).

R360.note: Table name resolved through a server-owned ALLOWED_TABLES map with the default preserved and bound values untouched, exactly what the contract calls for; the only-one-entry map and throw-on-unknown path are stated.

R361.note: Switching to EnyimMemcachedCore Store(StoreMode.Set, ...) frames the protocol and rejects space/control characters in keys, closing the injection; but the constructor now requires IMemcachedClient instead of Socket (every existing caller/DI registration breaks) and the value is stored via Enyim's transcoder with its own flags/encoding rather than raw flags=0 bytes, neither of which the write-up calls out.
